comments.comment: Ok so like this is really resonating because when I was in high school I was probably my theatre director’s favorite male actor, aside from the one who played the hero, while I was cast as the villain. If I auditioned, I was pretty much always in the show, partly because of my really good relationship with the director, but also just because I worked to develop my skills. I was really good at singing and acting because I worked really hard at it, and held a high standard for myself. I’m fully aware this makes me sound like a douchebag, but I’ve wasted too much of my life apologizing for myself lol  The thing that sucks about success and envy that Natalie managed to 360 no-scope is that I got such weird treatment from other theatre kids, especially the older ones. It was always passive aggressive quips and “you’re the favorite”. It always had such a venomous edge to it, and I’m recognizing now what that was. Since I had succeeded in winning the directors favor through building a relationship and honing my skills (i.e. working hard), I didn’t deserve the roles that I got because I was her favorite. It completely invalidated my accomplishments, and made them my fault somehow. And no one wanted to be my friend, even when I did my best to impress everybody so maybe they would like me.   So, yeah, being envied sucks. It’s the worst, because there’s nothing you can do to appease it aside from giving up what you have. And I ended up, you guessed it, apologizing for myself constantly and more or less being a total doormat to the older kids, and seeing myself as unworthy. Even when I succeeded I was still stuck in a really toxic mental state, in a way. Trying not to do that anymore, and after this video, I’m feeling reaffirmed in that. I hate that America (maybe other places too, just speaking from my own experience) promotes envy in such a way, because it really does poison everybody involved.  Anyways. 3:30 AM thoughts.
